section_summary: This section records the removal of companies from SCAP's restricted-concerns schedule and extensive revisions to Japan's Anti-Monopoly Law. It also covers disputes over cigarette-lighter export agencies, inquiries into private participation in Japan's tobacco monopoly, and the work of the Deconcentration Review Board. The final press release reports the board's recommendations, while the covering despatch cautions that deconcentration work was not entirely finished.

subfiles.title: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Removes specified companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.summary: SCAP cites earlier restriction orders and lists companies released from the schedule, including industrial, shipping, textile, mining, and trading concerns.

subfiles.title: Revision of Japanese Anti-Monopoly Law
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and analyzes amendments to Japan's Anti-Monopoly Law.
subfiles.summary: The despatch explains how a revised definition of competition affects foreign investment, international agreements, stock holdings, directorates, mergers, and transfers of businesses. It compares the enacted measure with November 1948 and February 1949 drafts and notes changes to filing requirements, enforcement, and penalties.

subfiles.title: Proposed Amendments to the Anti-Monopoly Law, opening page
subfiles.about: Proposes changes to the definitions of competition and rules for international agreements.
subfiles.summary: Defines competition and proposes registration of international trade agreements within thirty days.

subfiles.title: Bill to Amend the Law Relating to Prohibition of Private Monopolization and Methods of Preserving Fair Trade
subfiles.about: Sets out the enacted revisions to Japan's Anti-Monopoly Law article by article.
subfiles.summary: The bill revises the definition of competition and rules for international agreements, holding companies, securities ownership, interlocking directorates, mergers, and business transfers. It expands Fair Trade Commission procedures and remedies, revises fines and criminal penalties, and adds transitional provisions.

subfiles.title: Proposed Amendments to the Anti-Monopoly Law, remaining pages
subfiles.about: Continues the proposed amendments begun on page 366 after the intervening bill.
subfiles.summary: The draft addresses holding companies, corporate stock and debenture holdings, financial institutions, interlocking directorates, mergers, and transfers or leases of business assets. It proposes reporting and permission requirements for certain transactions.

subfiles.title: Trans Global Company's letter to the President
subfiles.about: Reports progress in resolving a dispute over Japanese cigarette-lighter exports.
subfiles.summary: Breen forwards MacArthur's reply and praises his handling of the trade dispute.

subfiles.title: MacArthur's reply to Trans Global Co.
subfiles.to: J. M. Breen, Trans Global Co.
subfiles.about: Addresses claims of exclusive rights to export Japanese camera-style cigarette lighters.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur rejects the trading company's claim to exclusive supply, identifies other manufacturers, promises to investigate delayed delivery, and explains export check prices.

subfiles.title: Correction to Anti-Monopoly Law translation
subfiles.about: Corrects the penalty amount in Article 110-2 of the transmitted translation.
subfiles.summary: Changes Article 110-2's penalty from twenty thousand to two hundred thousand yen.

subfiles.title: Report of Larus Agent in Tokyo Concerning Japanese Tobacco Monopoly
subfiles.from: J. K. Havemeyer, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records Larus and Brother's inquiry about reported British-American Tobacco negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Larus representatives report an agent's claim; Major Brickett agrees to seek information from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Telephone Conversation on British-American Tobacco Negotiations
subfiles.from: J. K. Havemeyer, Department of State
subfiles.about: Confirms that British-American Tobacco's negotiations had ended.
subfiles.summary: Blanton receives confirmation; the memorandum also notes separate China-American Leaf Tobacco talks.

subfiles.title: Complaint of Trans Global Company Regarding Exclusive Agency for Camera-type Cigarette Lighters
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the investigation and apparent resolution of the cigarette-lighter agency dispute.
subfiles.summary: SCAP found the claimed exclusive agency unapproved and invalid; Kyoei Trading retracted its claim.

subfiles.title: Request for Details on Deconcentration Cases
subfiles.about: Requests an update on company reorganizations and designated banks.
subfiles.summary: Seeks completed and pending reorganization details and probable Fair Trade Commission action on banks.

subfiles.title: Inquiry into Tobacco Monopoly Negotiations
subfiles.about: Requests details and policy assessment of proposed U.S. participation in Japan's tobacco monopoly.
subfiles.summary: The Department relays SCAP's account of ended British-American Tobacco talks and ongoing China-American Leaf Tobacco discussions. It raises concerns about monopoly ownership, public reaction, legislation, and conflict with competition policy.

subfiles.title: SCAP Press Release Announcing Completion of Work of Deconcentration Board
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP release and qualifies its account of completed deconcentration work.
subfiles.summary: The despatch corrects the release's case totals and identifies eleven companies still under consideration.

subfiles.title: Deconcentration Review Board Completes Task
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Far East Command, Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Announces completion of the board's recommendations and summarizes Japan's deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: The release names board members, reviews the dissolution of holding companies and other antimonopoly measures, and describes the board's review of designated operating companies. It reports recommendations for reorganization, lesser adjustments, referrals, and removal from designation.
